all.reason: The workload changed, not the VM: the translator no longer reads class files through ASM and its JavaScript generator is no longer stubbed out of the self-hosted build, so 'translator (self)' now translates a corpus about twice as large (both arms take ~2x as long: ParparVM 955 -> 1890ms, JDK 1.8 -> 3.0-3.75s on linux-x64). Translating a real application did not slow down: the hello row stayed in band on linux and macOS, arm64 hello got faster (9.5 -> 8.7s), and Windows x64's out-of-band hello RAM was the JDK arm swinging 832-987MB between rounds while ParparVM held 835-857MB.
